chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Do those who look at the behinds of women not fear that they will be tested with that regarding their own women?
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of men looking at the backs of women according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kulayni’s *Al-Kafi*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) employs the principle of *al-muthal* (reciprocity) to warn men that their gaze at other women’s backs invites a similar scrutiny of their own wives, reflecting the Shia emphasis on mutual privacy (*hurmah*) within the family unit. This ethical injunction extends beyond mere physical modesty to include the spiritual and social sanctity of the household, urging believers to guard their eyes as a means of preserving the dignity of their spouses.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Those who do not fear looking at the behinds of the women, they would be afflicted with that regarding their own womenfolk’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Do you not fear, when looking at women’s behind, for your women being looked in the same way.’”
